To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spin-coating of polymer blends results in the formation of a transient wetting-layer phase that undergoes a Rayleigh-Plateau-type instability, which results in phase separation and the formation of a final phase-separated thin polymer film.

spin-casting a polymer blend leads to a transient wetting morphology that is laterally phase separated, and that this phase separation is driven by an interfacial instability that leads to a final morphology that depends strongly on the blend composition.
the phase separation in thin polymer films occurs in two stages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental understanding of the development and control of structure and morphology in thin polymer-blend films, and how this affects device performance.
understanding the fundamental physics and chemistry of the spin-coating of polymers and blends, and the resulting morphology.
understanding and controlling the development of morphology during the fabrication of thin films by spin-coating.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
spin-casting of thin mixed polymer films leads to a transient wetting-layer phase separation, which is followed by a lateral phase separation.

we have developed a fundamental understanding of how the phase separation of thin polymer blend films develops during spin-coating, and we have used this understanding to develop a new method to control the phase separation and thus the film structure, and thus to control the properties of the resulting devices.
spin coating is a very widely-used technique for making uniform films.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have established the mechanism for how thin polymer films phase-separate during the spin-coat process.

the spin-coating method is a powerful tool for creating thin polymer films and blends, and that the process of phase separation in such films is now well understood, so that it is possible to use this understanding in order to achieve the best morphology for the application of interest.
the interfacial instability of the wetting layer leads the phase-separation in the thin polymer-blend films, which is a new insight into the mechanism of spin coating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of phase separation in thin films is not a purely thermodynamic process; the dynamics are also crucial.

spin-coating is a surprisingly powerful tool for the self-assembly of thin polymer films, and can be used to create a variety of complex morphologies, not just the simple vertical stratification of the two components that was previously thought to be the only outcome.
the phase separation that occurs in spin-cast thin polymer blend films is a consequence of an interfacial instability.
